run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T12:22:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is firing because frontend's checkout route fails: POST /api/checkout and its gRPC child grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carried ERROR status from ~12:21-12:22 to ~12:30, ~82% of checkout attempts in 12:22-12:32 errored, and those spans took ~9.1-9.7 s instead of the ~0.53-0.61 s baseline. The failure originates one level down: checkout's client span HTTP POST to shipping and checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder both error at 9750 ms, and shipping's own server span /get-quote errors in exactly the same count (266.8 error spans each over 12:09-12:35), with shipping /get-quote p95 rising from 80-125 ms (11:55-12:22) to 2975-4587 ms for successful calls and 9750 ms for errors. Inside shipping, the slow part is its outbound HTTP POST to the quote service (span 'POST quote', same duration as /get-quote; deployment env QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080), not the rest of the handler: shipping's /ship-order stayed at 1.9 ms and every other checkout dependency (cart 91.7 ms, currency 84.0 ms, payment 81.3 ms, product-catalog 76.7 ms, empty-cart 250 ms, orders publish 1.9 ms) stayed normal. The quote service itself is healthy - p95 1.90-1.99 ms unchanged across the whole window, no ERROR status spans, both replicas logging 'Calculated quote' throughout - but it received only ~0.1158 req/s during the incident versus ~0.49-0.60 req/s at baseline, exactly the rate of shipping's *successful* quotes, while shipping kept issuing ~0.54 requests/s. So about 78-79% of the requests shipping sent toward quote never reached quote's handler, and the survivors were delayed by 1.4-5 s. That points to the request path between shipping and the quote Service (connection establishment/packet delivery, possibly DNS for the 'quote' hostname) rather than to any application in the chain. Container CPU throttling, pod crashes/restarts/OOM, resource-driven node pressure and a traffic surge are all contradicted by the data. The precise mechanism (packet loss/network fault versus DNS resolution delay) could not be proven: chaos-mesh is installed in the cluster but chaos experiment objects are not readable with the permitted resource kinds, and no DNS/network metrics exist in the queried Prometheus.

claims.text: At 12:22:06 the frontend's 5-minute span rate had ERROR status only on the checkout path: grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.102/s, POST 0.102/s, POST /api/checkout 0.102/s and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 0.102/s; every other frontend operation (GET, GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart, grpc AdService/CartService/ProductCatalogService/RecommendationService calls) had 0 ERROR rate.

The cumulative ERROR counter for frontend 'POST /api/checkout' was flat at 44 from 12:14 to 12:21, then 71 at 12:22, rising roughly 25-30 per minute to 323 at 12:30 and staying 323 at 12:31-12:34 (279 new error spans). The shipping '/get-quote' ERROR counter first appeared at 27 at 12:22 and reached 279 at 12:30, flat afterwards.

Over 12:22-12:32, frontend 'POST /api/checkout' recorded 243.2 error spans against 51.7 non-error spans (~82% error ratio); 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' had identical error/non-error counts (243.2 / 51.7).

Error spans over 12:09-12:35 line up one-for-one along the checkout-to-shipping path: shipping 'POST quote' 266.8 and '/get-quote' 266.8, checkout 'HTTP POST' 266.8 and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 266.8, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, POST, POST /api/checkout and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 287.4 each, and frontend-proxy 'ingress' 297.7 with 'router frontend egress' 289.5.

Shipping '/get-quote' p95 was 79.8-125 ms for STATUS_CODE_UNSET from 11:55 to 12:22, then 2975 ms at 12:24 and 4399.9-4587.5 ms through 12:34; STATUS_CODE_ERROR p95 was 9750 ms at every point from 12:24 to 12:34.

At 12:30 shipping '/get-quote' ran 0.4246 errors/s against 0.1158 successes/s. Its histogram shows every error between 5000 and 10000 ms (0 above 10000 ms, 0 below 5000 ms), while successes are mixed: 0.0425/s <=10 ms, 0.0540/s <=50 ms, 0.0656/s <=200 ms, 0.0772/s <=1400 ms and 0.1158/s <=5000 ms.

The quote service stayed fast and error-free: its p95 was 1.900-1.995 ms at every 2-minute step from 12:00 to 12:34 (1.932 ms at 12:10 baseline, 1.921 ms at 12:30), all its spans carried STATUS_CODE_UNSET only ('POST /getquote', 'calculate-quote', '{closure}'), and at 12:30 its 'POST /getquote' bucket distribution put 0.1119 of 0.1158/s at <=2 ms.

Quote's received request rate ('POST /getquote') fell from 0.5222/s at 12:24 baseline to 0.1889, 0.0630, 0.0815, 0.1158, 0.0795/s at 12:24-12:31, i.e. to 0.1158/s, while shipping kept issuing the same total number of '/get-quote' requests (0.4902-0.60/s successful at baseline; at 12:30 0.4246 errors/s + 0.1158 successes/s = 0.5404/s).

Shipping's '/ship-order' span, which does not use the quote call, stayed at p95 1.9 ms at 12:10 (baseline) and 1.9 ms at 12:30, with a call rate of 0.1158/s equal to shipping's successful /get-quote rate.

At 12:30 checkout's spans other than the shipping call were normal: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart p95 91.7 ms, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert 84.0 ms, oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 81.3 ms, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 76.7 ms, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 250 ms, 'orders publish' 1.9 ms; only 'HTTP POST' (to shipping) 3650 ms success / 9750 ms error, 'prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart' 9682 ms and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 4550 ms success / 9750 ms error were inflated.
Currency p95 stayed 61.2-82.5 ms and product-catalog p95 stayed 1.95-1.97 ms at every step from 11:55 to 12:33, and neither service appears among the services with ERROR spans in the window.

Frontend latency at 12:30 vs 12:10 baseline is inflated only on the checkout route: POST /api/checkout 605.7->9683.6 ms, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 528.0->9683.6 ms, POST 380.5->8776.5 ms, while GET / 178.8->140.0, GET /api/cart 270.0->186.2, GET /api/data 196.0->160.5, GET /api/products/{productId} 158.2->138.6, GET /api/recommendations 467.5->373.8 and GET /api/cart (route) 240.4->199.6 ms stayed at or below baseline.

Per-service ERROR rates from 11:55 to 12:38 were elevated only for checkout (0.230-0.857/s), shipping (0.230-0.852/s), frontend (0.417-1.745/s) and frontend-proxy (0.224-0.865/s); cart, payment, currency, product-catalog, accounting, fraud-detection and recommendation were 0 or at the ~0.0037/s flagd EventStream/Resolve noise seen before the incident, and email/shipping-other-operations showed none.

All otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts, including shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 (start 2026-11-15T11:45:58Z), quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt (both 11:45:56Z), checkout-5dccddf8bb-vz2zd and frontend-675fd7b5c5-d2vwq.

The 63 events returned for otel-demo with timestamps 12:20:08-12:30:08 are all Normal 'Updated' events ('Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource') for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt and shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9; none of them is Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy, Failed or a controller SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete.

Shipping is a single-replica deployment whose container env sets QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 and which runs with cpu limit 5m / request 1m, memory limit 15Mi; the quote deployment has 2 replicas also with cpu limit 5m; its Service exposes two ready endpoints, 100.96.4.53 on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e and 100.96.2.155 on node i-0f88eaa39b314c60b, port 8080.

Both quote replicas kept serving requests during the incident: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b logged 37 'Calculated quote' lines between 12:20:02 and 12:30:05 and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt logged 28 'Calculated quote' lines between 12:20:03 and 12:30:07.

Container CPU throttling did not increase during the incident: throttled-period ratio for shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 was 7.3-11.2% at 12:00-12:21 and 5.8-7.2% at 12:22-12:33, for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b 8.1-11.8% then 4.8-8.6%, and for quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt 6.0-11.8% then 3.8-9.1%; CPU usage at 12:30 was 0.996 millicores (shipping) and 0.288/0.303 millicores (quote pods).

In the newest 200 of 1576 shipping log lines between 12:26:28 and 12:30:36, 'Requesting quote' lines outnumber the 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' pairs, i.e. many quote requests were started without a completing send in that sample; the container logged no error text.

Checkout's logs still show completed orders during the incident (e.g. at 12:30:04-12:30:07 '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent to ...', 'Successful to write message'), so part of the traffic succeeded while the rest failed.

The demo flagd configuration contains no shipping or quote flag; all relevant failure flags (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, adHighCpu, adManualGc, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) declare defaultVariant 'off'.

The newest shipping trace sample available (spans timestamped 12:06:07-12:06:12, before the incident) shows the healthy shape of this path: /get-quote 17.0 ms, its child 'POST quote' 16.8 ms, /ship-order 32-55 us, all with status_state not_recorded, inside checkout/frontend traces that returned http.status_code 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Chaos-mesh is installed and running cluster-wide during the window: chaos-controller-manager (3 replicas) and chaos-daemon pods on nodes i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, i-0f88eaa39b314c60b, i-0c466d0294b17ee91 and i-057763a5797b8b461, all Running/Ready/0 restarts since 2026-11-14T12:43:51Z.

Primary cause: the frontend alert is a downstream symptom of a fault on the HTTP request path between the shipping pod and the quote Service. Shipping's outbound 'POST quote' call (QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080) took 3.6-9.8 s or failed, so ~79% of GetQuote calls errored, checkout's PlaceOrder failed after ~9.1-9.8 s and frontend's /api/checkout errored. The failure is not in quote's handler: quote stayed at ~2 ms p95 with no error spans, yet it received only ~0.1158 req/s (exactly shipping's success rate) instead of the ~0.54 req/s shipping issued, so most requests were lost or blocked before reaching quote's application code, and the survivors were delayed (1.4-5 s bucket mass) as expected from retransmission/connection-establishment delay.

Candidate mechanism A: an injected network fault (packet loss/delay) affecting the shipping pod's egress or the quote pods' ingress for the duration 12:21-12:30. Chaos-mesh controllers and per-node daemons are running in this cluster, both quote endpoints on two different nodes were affected equally (both still served the surviving 0.1158 req/s), and the delay distribution (mass at <=10 ms, 200-1400 ms, 1.4-5 s for successes, 5-10 s for errors) resembles TCP retransmission backoff rather than a fixed added latency. No chaos experiment object could be read with the permitted resource kinds, so this is not confirmed.

Candidate mechanism B: DNS resolution of the hostname 'quote' inside the shipping pod became slow/failing. Shipping resolves QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 and is the only service in this chain that performs a hostname lookup for a per-request HTTP call; shipping emits no dns.lookup spans (its only span names are /get-quote, POST quote, /ship-order), so resolver time would be hidden inside the 'POST quote' span. The observed ~4.5 s successful and 5-10 s failed durations are compatible with a 5 s resolver timeout plus retry, and DNS failures would also explain why quote never saw those requests. No DNS metric or resolver evidence was available to confirm this.

The quote service is not failing: p95 1.900-1.995 ms unchanged across 11:55-12:34, only STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, and both replicas logged 'Calculated quote' at their normal cadence throughout the incident. Its latency and error signals give no support for blaming quote's application.

Resource starvation is not supported: shipping was throttled in 5.8-7.2% of CFS periods during the incident versus 7.3-11.2% before it, quote pods similarly lower, and CPU usage was about 1.0 millicore (shipping) and 0.29-0.30 millicores (quote).

No pod-level disruption explains this: every otel-demo pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts (shipping, both quote replicas, checkout, frontend all started 11:45-11:47Z), and the 63 namespace events from 12:20:08 to 12:30:08 are all Normal 'Updated' events for the quote and shipping pods - no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy, Failed, SuccessfulCreate or SuccessfulDelete.

The other checkout dependencies were healthy at 12:30 (cart 91.7 ms, currency 84.0 ms, payment 81.3 ms, product-catalog 76.7 ms, empty-cart 250 ms, orders publish 1.9 ms) and currency/product-catalog p95 stayed flat all window, so the error path is specific to shipping's quote call.

No traffic surge: shipping's total /get-quote request rate was ~0.49-0.60/s before the incident and 0.5404/s at 12:30 (0.4246 errors + 0.1158 successes), and /ship-order's rate merely tracks the successful quote rate.

Rejected: a failure inside the quote service (application error, slow handler or per-pod defect) caused the checkout errors. Quote's p95 was unchanged at ~1.9 ms with no error spans and both replicas continued logging successful calculations while shipping's client-side calls failed.

Rejected: CPU throttling of the shipping or quote containers caused the multi-second quote calls. Throttled-period ratios were lower during the incident than before it for all three containers and CPU usage was ~1 millicore or less.

Rejected: a crash, OOM eviction or rollout of shipping/quote during the window explains it. All pods report Running/Ready with 0 restarts and unchanged start times, and the window's events are only Normal 'Updated' events.
Rejected: currency or product-catalog degradation propagated into the quote path. Their p95 stayed at 61-82 ms and 1.95-1.97 ms respectively with no ERROR spans in the window.

Rejected: a feature-flag-driven failure in shipping/quote. The flagd config defines no shipping or quote flag and all failure flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, etc.) are at defaultVariant 'off'; the only flagd-related error spans present are the ~0.0037/s EventStream/Resolve noise seen both before and during the incident.

Confirm or exclude the network-fault hypothesis by reading chaos-mesh experiment objects (NetworkChaos/DNSChaos) and chaos-controller-manager logs for 12:20-12:32 against shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 or the quote pods (100.96.4.53, 100.96.2.155); the chaos custom resources are not readable with the resource kinds available in this Run.

To separate mechanism A from B, compare CoreDNS query latency/logs and the shipping pod's /etc/resolv.conf with another pod on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, and read the exact client error of a failing shipping span (dial/timeout/resolver) once Jaeger holds traces from 12:21-12:30.

gaps: No chaos experiment object could be read: the permitted Kubernetes kinds do not include chaos-mesh custom resources, so an active NetworkChaos/DNSChaos targeting shipping or quote is unverified (chaos-controller-manager and chaos-daemon pods are merely present).

No DNS or network telemetry exists in the queried Prometheus (metric-name lookups for dns/coredns/cilium/network patterns returned nothing), so I cannot distinguish a packet-loss/connection fault from a DNS resolution delay on the shipping->quote path.

Jaeger holds no traces for the incident window: searches for checkout and shipping in 12:15-12:38 returned no data, and the newest sampled spans are timestamped 12:06:07-12:06:12, so the exact error status text/error details of the failing /get-quote and HTTP POST spans are unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not present in the Prometheus rules endpoint (rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing), so the alert's expression and its 'current: 1.1111' value could not be verified against the metric.
Shipping's container logs contain no error text for the failed quote calls, so the client-side error (dial timeout vs reset vs resolver failure) is unknown.
A NetworkPolicy read for otel-demo returned no objects and that view is not citable (status no_data), so I cannot state that no policy change occurred on the shipping->quote path.
No load-generator span-duration series exist in this Prometheus (query returned no data), so there is no independent control showing whether other pods' pod-to-pod latency was also affected.

accounting's p95 rose from its 3.5-4.2 s baseline to 15000 ms at 12:26-12:28 and 5000 ms at 12:29 with zero error spans; it is not on the checkout path and I could not tie it to this cause, so it remains an unplaced observation.
frontend's 'POST /api/checkout' ERROR counter was already 44 before 12:14, i.e. earlier error spans predate this incident; their cause and timing are outside the evidence gathered.

The incident's end can only be bounded loosely: the error counters stop increasing after ~12:30 and the newest Prometheus sample is ~12:35, so the exact recovery time is unknown; POST /api/checkout errors in 12:14-12:30 include earlier accumulated errors.
next_steps: Inspect chaos-mesh NetworkChaos/DNSChaos resources and chaos-controller-manager logs for 12:20-12:32 to confirm or rule out fault injection on the shipping pod or quote endpoints.
Check CoreDNS health/latency and the shipping pod's resolver configuration, and compare fresh-connection DNS behaviour from another pod on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e.
Once Jaeger retains 12:21-12:30 traces, read the shipping '/get-quote' and 'POST quote' error spans' status/error text to identify the client error (timeout, refusal, resolver failure).
Review cilium/CNI and node network counters for node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e (shipping) toward 100.96.4.53 and 100.96.2.155 for the same interval.
Separately review accounting's p95 jump to 15 s at 12:26-12:28 to determine whether it is independent noise or a second problem.

Both quote replicas kept serving requests during the incident: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b logged 37 'Calculated quote' lines between 12:20:02 and 12:30:05 and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt logged 28 'Calculated quote' lines between 12:20:03 and 12:30:07.

Container CPU throttling did not increase during the incident: throttled-period ratio for shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 was 7.3-11.2% at 12:00-12:21 and 5.8-7.2% at 12:22-12:33, for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b 8.1-11.8% then 4.8-8.6%, and for quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt 6.0-11.8% then 3.8-9.1%; CPU usage at 12:30 was 0.996 millicores (shipping) and 0.288/0.303 millicores (quote pods).

In the newest 200 of 1576 shipping log lines between 12:26:28 and 12:30:36, 'Requesting quote' lines outnumber the 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' pairs, i.e. many quote requests were started without a completing send in that sample; the container logged no error text.

Checkout's logs still show completed orders during the incident (e.g. at 12:30:04-12:30:07 '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent to ...', 'Successful to write message'), so part of the traffic succeeded while the rest failed.

The demo flagd configuration contains no shipping or quote flag; all relevant failure flags (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, adHighCpu, adManualGc, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) declare defaultVariant 'off'.

The newest shipping trace sample available (spans timestamped 12:06:07-12:06:12, before the incident) shows the healthy shape of this path: /get-quote 17.0 ms, its child 'POST quote' 16.8 ms, /ship-order 32-55 us, all with status_state not_recorded, inside checkout/frontend traces that returned http.status_code 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Chaos-mesh is installed and running cluster-wide during the window: chaos-controller-manager (3 replicas) and chaos-daemon pods on nodes i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, i-0f88eaa39b314c60b, i-0c466d0294b17ee91 and i-057763a5797b8b461, all Running/Ready/0 restarts since 2026-11-14T12:43:51Z.

hypothesis.text: Primary cause: the frontend alert is a downstream symptom of a fault on the HTTP request path between the shipping pod and the quote Service. Shipping's outbound 'POST quote' call (QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080) took 3.6-9.8 s or failed, so ~79% of GetQuote calls errored, checkout's PlaceOrder failed after ~9.1-9.8 s and frontend's /api/checkout errored. The failure is not in quote's handler: quote stayed at ~2 ms p95 with no error spans, yet it received only ~0.1158 req/s (exactly shipping's success rate) instead of the ~0.54 req/s shipping issued, so most requests were lost or blocked before reaching quote's application code, and the survivors were delayed (1.4-5 s bucket mass) as expected from retransmission/connection-establishment delay.

Candidate mechanism A: an injected network fault (packet loss/delay) affecting the shipping pod's egress or the quote pods' ingress for the duration 12:21-12:30. Chaos-mesh controllers and per-node daemons are running in this cluster, both quote endpoints on two different nodes were affected equally (both still served the surviving 0.1158 req/s), and the delay distribution (mass at <=10 ms, 200-1400 ms, 1.4-5 s for successes, 5-10 s for errors) resembles TCP retransmission backoff rather than a fixed added latency. No chaos experiment object could be read with the permitted resource kinds, so this is not confirmed.

Candidate mechanism B: DNS resolution of the hostname 'quote' inside the shipping pod became slow/failing. Shipping resolves QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 and is the only service in this chain that performs a hostname lookup for a per-request HTTP call; shipping emits no dns.lookup spans (its only span names are /get-quote, POST quote, /ship-order), so resolver time would be hidden inside the 'POST quote' span. The observed ~4.5 s successful and 5-10 s failed durations are compatible with a 5 s resolver timeout plus retry, and DNS failures would also explain why quote never saw those requests. No DNS metric or resolver evidence was available to confirm this.

recommendation.text: Confirm or exclude the network-fault hypothesis by reading chaos-mesh experiment objects (NetworkChaos/DNSChaos) and chaos-controller-manager logs for 12:20-12:32 against shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 or the quote pods (100.96.4.53, 100.96.2.155); the chaos custom resources are not readable with the resource kinds available in this Run.

To separate mechanism A from B, compare CoreDNS query latency/logs and the shipping pod's /etc/resolv.conf with another pod on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e, and read the exact client error of a failing shipping span (dial/timeout/resolver) once Jaeger holds traces from 12:21-12:30.

counter_evidence.text: The quote service is not failing: p95 1.900-1.995 ms unchanged across 11:55-12:34, only STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, and both replicas logged 'Calculated quote' at their normal cadence throughout the incident. Its latency and error signals give no support for blaming quote's application.

Resource starvation is not supported: shipping was throttled in 5.8-7.2% of CFS periods during the incident versus 7.3-11.2% before it, quote pods similarly lower, and CPU usage was about 1.0 millicore (shipping) and 0.29-0.30 millicores (quote).

No pod-level disruption explains this: every otel-demo pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts (shipping, both quote replicas, checkout, frontend all started 11:45-11:47Z), and the 63 namespace events from 12:20:08 to 12:30:08 are all Normal 'Updated' events for the quote and shipping pods - no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy, Failed, SuccessfulCreate or SuccessfulDelete.

The other checkout dependencies were healthy at 12:30 (cart 91.7 ms, currency 84.0 ms, payment 81.3 ms, product-catalog 76.7 ms, empty-cart 250 ms, orders publish 1.9 ms) and currency/product-catalog p95 stayed flat all window, so the error path is specific to shipping's quote call.

No traffic surge: shipping's total /get-quote request rate was ~0.49-0.60/s before the incident and 0.5404/s at 12:30 (0.4246 errors + 0.1158 successes), and /ship-order's rate merely tracks the successful quote rate.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: a failure inside the quote service (application error, slow handler or per-pod defect) caused the checkout errors. Quote's p95 was unchanged at ~1.9 ms with no error spans and both replicas continued logging successful calculations while shipping's client-side calls failed.

Rejected: CPU throttling of the shipping or quote containers caused the multi-second quote calls. Throttled-period ratios were lower during the incident than before it for all three containers and CPU usage was ~1 millicore or less.

Rejected: a crash, OOM eviction or rollout of shipping/quote during the window explains it. All pods report Running/Ready with 0 restarts and unchanged start times, and the window's events are only Normal 'Updated' events.
Rejected: currency or product-catalog degradation propagated into the quote path. Their p95 stayed at 61-82 ms and 1.95-1.97 ms respectively with no ERROR spans in the window.

Rejected: a feature-flag-driven failure in shipping/quote. The flagd config defines no shipping or quote flag and all failure flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, etc.) are at defaultVariant 'off'; the only flagd-related error spans present are the ~0.0037/s EventStream/Resolve noise seen both before and during the incident.
